_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401909976.text: Toronto arrive on the second night of a back-to-back after blowing a 22-point home lead in a 98-93 loss to Boston. They are still without Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard and have used six starting lineups in ten games. Philadelphia are coming off a 22-point home loss to the Celtics, but both LeBron James (back) and Joel Embiid (foot) are questionable, with the Sixers openly managing their workloads before Indiana and Brooklyn. A deflating collapse plus fatigue leans the mood toward Philadelphia, as long as their stars play.

401909977.text: Washington have lost five straight after Wednesday's 114-101 loss in Indiana, and they play this game on a back-to-back. Anthony Davis has already called out the team's defense. Detroit beat them 122-111 only three days ago and have won seven of the last nine meetings. The Pistons are missing Jalen Duren and Isaiah Joe, but confidence and freshness both lean toward Detroit.

401909978.text: Both teams are rolling. Minnesota have won four straight and are 5-2 without Anthony Edwards, who is out for up to two months after knee surgery; Ayo Dosunmu has averaged 21.6 points in his place. Dallas have won three straight, with Cooper Flagg's 43 against Indiana. This game starts a three-game road trip that continues in Cleveland and Boston. There is a mild subplot: Kyrie Irving was rumoured as a Wolves target last summer. The mental picture is balanced, with a slight lean to Minnesota's rested home side.

401909979.text: This is the first meeting since the summer trade that sent Miles Bridges to Phoenix and Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale to Charlotte. So far it looks lopsided toward the Hornets: Allen is shooting nearly 47% from three, while Bridges has a deeply negative net rating. Charlotte just snapped a six-game skid in Cleveland but are still without Brandon Miller, Dennis Schroder and Kon Knueppel, and this game opens a four-game road trip. Former-team motivation runs both ways, and the depleted roster leans this toward Phoenix.

401909296.text: New York come in deflated after a 115-107 home loss to Cleveland ended their five-game hold over the Cavs. Karl-Anthony Towns played through a sore calf amid stalled extension talks and trade chatter. Indiana snapped a losing run by beating Washington but are still only 1-5 at home. Rick Carlisle has hinted that Tyrese Haliburton could have an update in about ten days, and he spent the week fuming at the officials. The mood edges slightly toward Indiana's home bounce, but this is close to neutral.

401909297.text: Milwaukee's slide reached nine straight with losses to the Knicks (by 32) and the Lakers. Taylor Jenkins has admitted "what we're doing right now is not working", and Kyle Kuzma is publicly demanding urgency. Tyler Herro is back and scored 27 against the Lakers. Orlando just closed a 2-2 West trip with their first winning streak of the season, with Franz Wagner scoring 30-plus in three straight. Despite a long list of absentees, including Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs, the Magic carry the better mood into an NBA Cup home game.

401909298.text: Cleveland bought some breathing room by winning at Madison Square Garden behind James Harden's season-high 32. That came days after Marc Stein said Kenny Atkinson's job needed "a very close eye". Miami open a five-game homestand after a 3-2 West trip. Giannis Antetokounmpo is playing through a sprained wrist and is still answering Doc Rivers' public jab at his basketball IQ. The Heat's homecoming and Giannis's edge lean slightly toward Miami, but Cleveland's urgency keeps it close.

401909299.text: Chicago have lost eight straight, are 0-4 at home, and blew a 22-point lead to San Antonio on Wednesday. They also lost No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson to a hand injury, though Norman Powell is expected back from back spasms. Atlanta had three days to reset after the Lakers ended their four-game win streak, and this NBA Cup game opens a three-game trip. The mental lean is toward Atlanta; a Bulls team that keeps blowing leads is fragile late in games.

401909300.text: New Orleans are in freefall. They lost by a franchise-record 51 to Golden State and then by 34 at home to Brooklyn, with the home crowd booing. That is their worst three-game stretch in franchise history, and opinion pieces are already floating a fire sale. Memphis have their own wobble: four losses in five after a 6-0 start, the latest a near-miss in Denver. A team this demoralised, playing at home, leans toward Memphis.

401909301.text: Utah are 1-11 and badly short-handed, with Lauri Markkanen (hand fractures) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (MCL) out for weeks. Will Hardy says the late-game collapses are no coincidence. Houston beat Golden State, but Marcus Smart was ejected for a punch and could face discipline, a possible distraction. Rookie Darryn Peterson's run of four straight 20-point games gives Utah something to play for. The mood still leans heavily toward Houston.

401909302.text: Golden State's eight-game win streak ended in Houston. Worse, Stephen Curry left with abdominal soreness and went for an MRI, and Steve Kerr said "concern is high". The Kristaps Porzingis standoff, with the Warriors withholding salary and exploring trades, adds noise on the second leg of a five-game trip. San Antonio extended their streak to ten by rallying from 22 down in Chicago, though Devin Vassell is still out. Curry's status is the key; the mental lean is clearly toward the Spurs.

401909303.text: Sacramento's locker room is visibly frustrated at 1-10. Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. said "I'm not a loser, so it's not fun". De'Andre Hunter called the frustration "very high", and Zach LaVine asked for unity "from the front office down". Doug Christie is in the final guaranteed year of his deal, and Domantas Sabonis trade talk lingers. Portland just beat Oklahoma City even without Ja Morant. The Kings could respond with pride at home, but the turmoil leans this toward Portland.

401909304.text: The Clippers are 2-8 after a 23-point loss in Phoenix, with Bradley Beal yet to play. The one hopeful note is that Brandon Ingram is "pretty close" to his debut after heel surgery. Oklahoma City arrive having lost back-to-back games in Portland and are thin: Ajay Mitchell, Jaylin Williams, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace were all listed out. Both teams have reasons to be irritable. An Ingram debut would give the Clippers a lift, but OKC's urge to bounce back is the stronger pull.
